Brand & Editor Guideline · V1.0

Built by Heroes.
Felt by Millions.

This is not a moodboard. It is the rulebook every Hook Hero video is cut against — so that a reel still looks like us after three different editors have touched it.

9:16 · Reels & Shorts DACH · Finance & Real Estate Premiere Pro · After Effects

01 — Brand Core

What we stand for

Hook Hero makes content for financial advisors, insurance brokers and real estate professionals in the German-speaking market. That audience is buried in agency promises every single day. Our antidote is proof instead of claims.

Show, don't tell

Every agency tells you what it can do. We show it. Real sites, real videos, real numbers — in that order.

Hook before polish

A video nobody finishes is worth nothing. Attention comes before aesthetics — and aesthetics is what holds it.

The client is the hero

We are the tool, not the main character. The lightning belongs to the client, not to us.

The metaphor behind the brand: cape and lightning bolt. The cape stands for cover — we take on what the client cannot do alone. The bolt stands for speed and impact. Together they set the core visual rule: a calm base, one sharp impulse. That principle governs every color field, every cut and every animation in this document.

02 — Voice

How we sound

Second person, short sentences, numbers first. We sound like an operator who knows the business — not like an agency reading its own portfolio out loud.

How we write

"From €10,000 to €100,000 in monthly revenue."

"Websites that sell — not just look good."

"2.37× cheaper leads. Here's the screenshot."

"Content without strategy is just noise."

Never

"We are your innovative partner for holistic digital solutions."

"Leverage synergies", "full-service", "360° approach"

"Maybe", "potentially", "could help"

Corporate distance. We always address the viewer directly.

Rules for on-screen text

Maximum seven words per on-screen line. No exclamation mark chains. Numbers always as digits (120,000 €, never "one hundred twenty thousand"). If the video is in German, follow German conventions: German quotation marks („…"), period as thousands separator, comma as decimal separator. Never mix the two systems inside one video.

03 — Logo

The mark

The H with cape and bolt. It exists in exactly one color version: the cyan-to-blue gradient. On light or colored surfaces it is set in a single flat color — never recolored.

✓ Primary · on black
✓ On deep navy
✓ Single color on light
× Never on the gradient

Clear space & minimum size

Keep clear space of 50 % of the logo height on all four sides. Nothing enters that zone — no text, no caption, no frame edge. Minimum sizes: 24 px digital, 40 px in a 1080×1920 video (roughly 3.7 % of the width).

Allowed
  • Scaling — always proportional, hold Shift.
  • As a watermark at 60–75 % opacity, top right, below the safe zone.
  • As a full-frame element in the outro, with glow.
Forbidden
  • Stretching, rotating, mirroring, or applying effect presets.
  • Placing it on busy footage without darkening underneath.
  • Adding drop shadows, outlines or a second color.
  • Sitting next to third-party logos without full clear space.

04 — Color System

Colors

The palette comes straight out of the logo. It is deliberately narrow: a dark ground, a cyan-to-blue gradient for energy, a blue-biased grey for everything quiet — and exactly one warm signal color reserved for results.

Click any swatch to copy its value to the clipboard.

The 70/25/5 rule

70 % of the frame is dark ground (Deep Navy or Void Black). 25 % is type in Ice White and Steel. 5 % is cyan-blue. The moment more than a fifth of the frame glows, the cyan loses its force and the video starts to look like a template.

Flash #FFD24A does not count toward that split — it is an exception, not a palette member. It appears at exactly one point per video: on the number that carries the proof ("120,000 € in monthly revenue"). Two yellow moments in one video cancel each other out.

Fallback rule: If Anton is unavailable in an application, fall back to Archivo Black — never to Impact, Bebas Neue or a system default. If Montserrat Black is unavailable, Archivo Black is the caption substitute.

06 — The Hook

The first three seconds

We are called Hook Hero. If anything in this document is non-negotiable, it is this. The first three seconds decide the reach of the entire video — everything after that only decides the conversion.

0.0 s

Picture first, sound second

Frame 1 already shows a face or a movement — never a title screen, never a logo, never black. The first caption is on screen by 0.2 s at the latest.

0–1 s

The claim

One sentence, seven words maximum, that opens a tension: a number, a contradiction, or a mistake the audience is making. No "hi", no "in this video".

1–2 s

The visual proof

Cut to whatever backs the claim: dashboard, screenshot, number, result. The proof is visible before it is explained.

2–3 s

The promise

What the viewer gets for staying. The hook ends here — the first scene change must have happened before 3.0 s.

Hard limits

No intro branding before the hook. No music lead-in over an empty frame. No question that can be answered "no" and swiped away. If you watch your own hook twice and want to scroll on the second time, it is not finished.

07 — Caption System

Captions

For us captions are not an accessibility feature, they are the primary design element. Around 80 % of viewers watch on mute — the text carries the message, the picture carries the credibility.

Safe zone · platform UI
2.37× cheaper
leads
Safe zone · caption & CTA
ParameterValue
TypefaceMontserrat Black 900
Size (1080×1920)76–88 px
Base color#EAF6FF
Active word color#00CAF2
Stroke10–14 px · #000D1A
Shadownone
Position56 % of frame height
Words per linemax. 3
Lines at oncemax. 2
Alignmentcentered
Tracking−1 %

The active word

In each caption block exactly one word is set in Hero Cyan — the word that carries the meaning. Not the verb, not the article: the word you want remembered. It switches in sync with the speech, not on a fixed interval. If a block has no word worth highlighting, it stays fully white.

When a number is spoken, highlight the number and not the unit: "120,000 € in monthly revenue" — and in that one case use Flash instead of Cyan.

Rhythm

Captions appear word by word or in pairs, never as a whole sentence at once. Entry: hard cut, or a 60 ms scale from 96 % to 100 %. No fades, no bounce, no typewriter. A block holds for at least 400 ms.

Building them in Premiere & After Effects

Captions are not rebuilt per video. The basis is the .mogrt template from After Effects in the Essential Graphics panel. It exposes typeface, stroke, position and the cyan toggle for the active word as editable parameters. Editing the template inside a project only changes it locally — changes to the master go through Gio.

Premiere's auto-transcription is allowed as a starting point (Text panel → Transcript → Create captions). After that the style must be switched to our master style and the line breaks set by hand to three words maximum. Raw auto-captions never ship.

08 — Frame

Frame & safe zones

Instagram and TikTok lay their own interface over our video. Anything inside the marked zones is invisible in the real feed, no matter how good it looks in the editing timeline.

ZoneArea at 1080 × 1920
Top (profile, status bar)0 – 270 px · keep clear
Bottom (caption, CTA, audio)1500 – 1920 px · keep clear
Right (action buttons)from 940 px · footage only, no text
Left (margin)0 – 60 px · footage only, no text
Safe text area60 – 940 px × 270 – 1500 px
Caption baselineapprox. 1075 px (56 %)
Logo watermarkx 880 px · y 300 px · 40 px wide

Framing

Talking head: eyes on the upper third line, headroom tight. Do not waste space above the head — the frame is tall, not wide. Screenshots and dashboards are never shown full-frame; zoom to the relevant section and add a 2 px Hero Cyan border so it reads clearly as evidence.

09 — Editing & Motion

Pace

Our editing is fast but not frantic. The difference: pace follows the speech, frantic follows a metronome.

Cut frequency

Seconds 0–10: 2.0 s per shot maximum.

From second 10: 3.5 s maximum, with a visual change (b-roll, zoom, graphic) at least every 4 s.

Every pause in speech longer than 300 ms gets cut out.

Movement

Zoom punch of 8 % maximum, 120–180 ms, ease-out. Always on a stressed syllable, never on a random point.

Camera moves in b-roll: slow and in one direction. No Ken Burns back-and-forth.

Permitted transitions

Hard cut (the default, roughly 90 % of all transitions). Whip pan on a real change of location. A 2-frame cyan flash — only on the transition into the proof section, once per video maximum. Nothing else. No effect-library presets, no glitches, no spins, no lens flares, no shake on every beat.

Premiere / After Effects split

Premiere Pro is the timeline: cutting, pacing, captions, audio, Lumetri, export. After Effects is the workbench: graphics, number animations, screenshot frames, logo outro, tracking. AE pieces come back into the timeline as .mogrt files — use Dynamic Link only when a piece genuinely has to change per video.

Motion is set in AE through the Graph Editor, not with default keyframes: ease-out at roughly 75 % influence on the final keyframe. Warp Stabilizer only on footage that truly needs it — it costs edge sharpness.

Motion principle

Anything that moves follows the lightning logic: fast in, immediately still. Elements never accelerate on entry — they decelerate. In practice: ease-out, 120–180 ms, no overshoot, no bounce. Nothing in a Hook Hero video wobbles.

10 — Look

Grading

The look is restrained. It should lift the footage, not announce itself as a filter. The target is clean, cool and contrasty — a picture that reads as office and competence, not travel vlog.

StepTarget
White balanceslightly cool, 200–400 K below neutral
Contrast+8 to +12
Black pointlifted to approx. 4 % (no pure black in frame)
Shadow tinttoward blue, very subtle
Saturation−5 global, skin tones untouched
Sharpening0.3 max — over-sharpening looks worse after Instagram compression
ToolLumetri Color in Premiere — no third-party plugins
OrderBasic → Creative → Curves → HSL → Vignette (off)
Forbiddenvignette, grain, teal-and-orange, film LUTs

Skin tones are the red line. If the blue tint starts making the client look unwell, it is too strong — then use no tint at all. A client who does not like how they look in their own video will not share it.

11 — Sound

Audio

Bad audio gets swiped away faster than bad picture. The voice is always the loudest element in the mix.

ElementValue
Integrated loudness−14 LUFS
True peak−1.0 dBTP max.
Voice−6 to −3 dB, EQ: low cut at 80 Hz
Music under voice−18 to −22 dB, ducking on
Music without voice−12 dB
Whooshes / impacts3 per video max., −10 dB
Music selectiondriving, no vocals, no drop clichés
ToolEssential Sound: Dialogue → Loudness → Auto-Match

Music starts at second 1 at the earliest and never before the first spoken word. A beat running ahead of the hook costs reach. For client videos one more rule applies: royalty-free or platform-licensed music only — when in doubt, ask, never assume.

12 — Outro

The close

The outro is short and always identical. It is the only moment where the brand itself takes the foreground.

Duration

1.5 to 2.0 seconds maximum. Anything longer gets swiped and drags down watch time.

Build

Void Black. Logo centered with cyan glow. Claim underneath in Anton, uppercase, Ice White.

CTA

One action, one sentence. "Link in bio" or "DM us HERO" — never both at once.

Important: On client videos the client owns the outro, not Hook Hero. Our logo appears there only on our own channels. On client accounts we stay invisible — watermark included.

File naming

Example: dkfinanz_altersvorsorge_v02_260827.mp4

Also deliver: the project via File → Project Manager → Collect Files and Copy (including the AE project and every .mogrt used), and a 1:1 crop (1080 × 1080) with the caption position corrected, when the brief calls for it.

14 — Rules

Do's & Don'ts

Always
  • Watch the video once on mute before delivery. Still understandable? Then the captions are right.
  • Check it on a phone, not just on the monitor.
  • Verify numbers and names against the brief — a misspelled client name is a total loss.
  • When in doubt, cut calmer rather than flashier.
  • Before exporting, render and play back at full resolution — never sign off in 1/2 preview mode.
  • Deliver two hook variants whenever the footage allows it.
Never
  • Shipping Premiere's default caption style (white type on a grey box) untouched.
  • Emoji in captions or on-screen text.
  • More than one accent color in the frame at the same time.
  • Music that sits on top of the speaker.
  • Text inside the safe zones.
  • Upscaled footage below 1080 px wide.
  • AI-generated material in client videos without sign-off.

15 — Delivery

Checklist

Run through this before every delivery. If one item is open, the video is not finished.

When in doubt: a calm base, one sharp impulse. If you cannot decide between two versions, take the quieter one — and spend the energy where the proof is.
